LS006.selection: On the sample, check lace contact at both openings and identify every point where lace is attached. Use LS005-142 if the reference brief you want has a V-shaped waistband.
LS006.approval: Approve the stretch of the body and lace together before choosing trim colors. Keep the two compositions separate in the artwork brief.

LS005-142.selection: Compare waist depth at center front and rear coverage with LS005 in the same size. Use the brief when the buyer wants more rear fabric with the V-waist treatment.
LS005-142.approval: Ask for a physical color match between lace and body. The listed color choices do not show whether the two components match under your selling photography.

LS005.selection: Confirm how far the point of the V sits below the side waist and how the lace behaves when the garment stretches. Compare LS005-142 when you want a brief cut in the same collection.
LS005.approval: Include an approved view of the front V and a separate lace color reference so the approval applies to the trim as well as the main fabric.

DYS323.selection: Compare DYS311 in the same size to isolate the difference between a bonded and stitched gusset as closely as possible. Record other panel differences before interpreting the result.
DYS323.approval: Inspect the bond perimeter before and after your agreed care procedure. Photograph any edge opening or lift and compare it with the approved sample.

DYS322.selection: Compare DYS302 if the buyer is choosing between bonded and stitched attachment in a low-rise thong. Record rear strip width and gusset position alongside the join type.
DYS322.approval: Inspect the gusset bond where it meets the narrow back. Ask the supplier to confirm that production will use the attachment approved on the sample.

DYS314.selection: Compare the front rise and seat coverage with DYS306. Both are in the seamless collection, but their silhouettes solve different coverage needs.
DYS314.approval: Assess waist roll while seated and compare the edge under the outer fabric selected for the range. Use the observed result when writing the listing.

DYS311.selection: Inspect the two rear panels and gusset stitching where the garment contacts the body. Bring a DYS323 sample to compare the different gusset attachment.
DYS311.approval: Specify whether any stitching visible on the approved sample is acceptable in the final garment, especially when listing the style as seamless.

DYS306.selection: Measure front and rear rise from the same reference points on DYS306 and DYS311. Compare rear coverage while standing and sitting before choosing a higher or lower cut.
DYS306.approval: Save a rear-view approval image so the panel placement and coverage are recorded even when product names are translated or shortened.

DYS302.selection: Compare DYS322 if a bonded gusset is an option. Check the location of the stitched section and visibility through the exact outer fabric selected for the trial.
DYS302.approval: Record the outer garment, underwear size and lighting with any visibility observation. Avoid extending the result to other outfits without checking them.

DYS301.selection: Compare DYS302 for a second low-rise option. Lay both samples flat and compare the depth of the front dip before evaluating side coverage on the body.
DYS301.approval: Keep a straight-on fit photo with the waist placement marked, so the approved V is distinguishable from the edge finish alone.

M008 Print.selection: Compare the placement and appearance of the supplied print with the plain M008 sample. Confirm the coverage and fit on both, especially if the print changes fabric handling.
M008 Print.approval: Approve the print on a cut and assembled front, where stretch and seam placement can change the appearance from the flat artwork.

M007 Print.selection: Use the M007 Print chart and physical garment to check the leg. The printed trunk and plain M007 boxer brief are different catalogue entries, so confirm dimensions separately.
M007 Print.approval: Approve an assembled sample with waistband and print colors together. Take the leg measurement from the specified seam rather than relying on the model family name.

M006 Print.selection: Compare M007 Print at the same labelled size to see how waistband and leg openings read on the body. Confirm the finished inseam for both.
M006 Print.approval: Approve the elastic color against the printed fabric under consistent light and record the acceptable shade reference for each component.

M005 Print.selection: Compare with plain M005 at the same size. Confirm each measured inseam and distinguish fit approval from approval of the print.
M005 Print.approval: Mark which motifs may cross the pouch seams and which must remain visible. Approve the assembled strike-off before signing off the repeat placement.

M004 Print.selection: Compare it with plain M004, which the catalogue describes as a no-fly trunk. Use independent fit records for the two entries.
M004 Print.approval: Approve the artwork repeat at the finished waistband and front-panel junction. Check that a color revision has not changed the version of trim you approved.

M003 Print.selection: If 3XL boxer briefs are part of the brief, include the upper size in the sample set. Compare pouch depth and leg opening to your base size after grading.
M003 Print.approval: Approve a print reference at both ends of your selected size run. A fixed repeat can sit differently on panels cut for different sizes.

M002 Print.selection: Review it against the plain M002, whose listed rise is regular. Measure front rise, back rise and inseam on both before allocating sizes.
M002 Print.approval: Check the motif placement along the extended leg and confirm whether major artwork elements must line up across left and right panels.

M001 Print.selection: Compare with the plain M001 brief only as a different silhouette. Confirm the leg coverage you want before assuming the two M001 names describe a single pattern.
M001 Print.approval: Specify waistband and print as separate approvals and include an assembled front photo so the agreed placement survives artwork revisions.

DYS229.selection: Compare DYS228 when the back shape or size range is the open decision. DYS229 is listed through XL, while the source for DYS228 extends through XXL.
DYS229.approval: Check zigzag stitching at rest and under the agreed stretch. Note any visible stitch change or discomfort on the physical sample.

DYS230.selection: Compare the rise and strap position with DYS226. Measure how the back strip meets the side straps and note the level of rear coverage on the actual sample.
DYS230.approval: Approve the waistband position separately from the back shape. A retailer's T-string label should match the photographs and cut it actually sells.

DYS228.selection: Compare its T-back dimensions with DYS229 and include the upper size when reviewing grade changes. Record back width on the physical sample.
DYS228.approval: Confirm how the back strip and side edges sit on the upper-size sample. Use the finished measurements in your range sheet.

DYS227.selection: Compare DYS225 if you are choosing between a broad waistband tanga and a high-waist thong. Record band width and rear coverage as distinct selection criteria.
DYS227.approval: Approve the elastic width and artwork repeat on the garment. Check the band's recovery and position before committing artwork to an elastic order.

DYS226.selection: Use DYS230 to see how the low-rise option changes waistband position. Check side strap length and front rise on both samples at the same size.
DYS226.approval: Record the desired rise and back shape separately. This lets a reviewer identify which feature needs a revision without switching the entire pattern.

DYS225.selection: Compare the rise with extra-high DYS205 and note that their listed size endpoints differ. Confirm the waist height on an upper-size sample if 2XL is planned.
DYS225.approval: Use the same garment measurement points on each size. Keep waistband height and total front rise as separate approval fields.

DYS224.selection: Compare it with DYS225 to decide whether to offer the higher rise alongside it. Request the same labelled size in both to review coverage on comparable samples.
DYS224.approval: Select a regular-rise base size and retain a separate approval for the 2XL grade. Confirm mixed color and size allocation on your quotation.

DYS223.selection: Compare DYS206 if your assortment is choosing between a conventional brief and bikini coverage. Verify waist position and leg-opening curve on both.
DYS223.approval: Approve the size allocation after inspecting upper-size seat coverage. Use the finished DYS223 sample to position the label away from pressure points.

DYS219.selection: Compare DYS210 to separate a high-cut opening from an extended-leg design. Both sit in the high-rise group and differ noticeably at the upper thigh.
DYS219.approval: Include sizes near both ends of the intended range when checking leg-opening curve and waist height. Confirm that your approved grade follows the desired proportions.

M008.selection: Compare the brief shape with M001 and record side depth and front opening in the intended base size. The waistband treatment is one of the selection points.
M008.approval: Inspect whether the inner waistband construction meets the buyer's label-placement and contact requirements before approving a branding method.

M007.selection: Ask the supplier to define the inseam measurement points and sample size. Compare the finished length with M005 using that same method.
M007.approval: Check the leg opening after movement and confirm how the pouch seam sits. Record the measurements and observations as separate pass criteria.

M006.selection: Measure the physical inseam and agree how the five-inch description is used in the buyer's copy. Compare M004 when the no-fly front is a stated priority.
M006.approval: Confirm the lining and main fabric separately. For any proposed recycled-polyester option, request the composition and order-specific supporting records before approving a claim.

M005.selection: Measure M005 and M007 from a shared inseam point. Approve the measurement before turning a nominal length into a consumer-facing dimension.
M005.approval: If recycled polyester is proposed, keep it as a separate material option until the supplier provides order-specific composition and traceability records.

M004.selection: Compare M003 if regular rise is the other option. Check front pouch depth and seam position in the same size and capture how the no-fly construction is described.
M004.approval: Mark waistband logo position on the assembled sample, especially if the logo must align with the front center of the no-fly pouch.

M003.selection: Compare the regular-rise silhouette with M004 and keep the exact pouch shape in the sample brief. Review the largest selected size if grading is part of the order.
M003.approval: Capture a measurement of the pouch and the leg opening at the upper size. This checks the fit plan before the brand prints a size chart.

M002.selection: Check inseam, leg opening and waistband tension alongside the shorter listed M007. Use matching measurement points and sample sizes on both.
M002.approval: Review the leg opening after movement and record whether the long leg stays where intended. Treat the result as a sample observation for your specific size.

M001.selection: Check what the approved tagless treatment will look like after adding your branding. Compare the cut with M008 in the same size before choosing the leg profile.
M001.approval: Agree where the required product information will appear and request a proof of the approved branding treatment on the physical garment.

DYS218.selection: Compare DYS208 for another regular-rise tanga. Look at the waistband and rear coverage separately so the logo choice does not determine fit selection.
DYS218.approval: Mark the lettering repeat, front-center placement and join position on approved artwork. Review the band on the garment at rest and under stretch.

DYS215.selection: Compare the waistband and leg profile with DYS214. Request same-size samples and record where the leg opening rests instead of relying on boxer versus boyshort naming.
DYS215.approval: Check waistband height and hold with the garment in the intended position. Confirm artwork dimensions only after agreeing the visible elastic area.

DYS214.selection: Compare DYS215 if a wide waist treatment is also under consideration. Evaluate the short-leg opening against the intended leg coverage and edge feel.
DYS214.approval: Keep the finished short-leg measurements and photographic reference with the sample record. They give the final listing a more reliable shape description than the category term alone.

DYS210.selection: Compare DYS219 to see the difference between extended coverage and a high-cut leg opening. Confirm the intended thigh coverage on the same size first.
DYS210.approval: Measure leg opening and extension independently. A change to either can affect where the hem sits under the outer garment selected for testing.

DYS208.selection: Lay it beside DYS218 and compare back width at the same point below the waistband. Confirm whether the labeled tanga coverage matches your retailer's description.
DYS208.approval: Use a rear-view photo of the approved garment to guide the product description. Record rear panel width separately from side depth.

DYS206.selection: Compare DYS202 as another regular-rise cotton reference. Check the shape of the leg opening, side depth and waistband on both before choosing the base pattern.
DYS206.approval: Record the finished leg opening with the garment laid flat and the measurement method stated. Review the edge against the intended wearing position on the sample.

DYS205.selection: Compare DYS225 to see how much rise the extra-high version adds at the chosen size. Request separate measurements for front and back.
DYS205.approval: Review the waistband position when seated as well as standing. Confirm the waist treatment before approving any logo or woven label placement.

DYS204.selection: Compare DYS230 if the plan also includes a T-string. Measure the back strip and side straps, and use photos to show how the two silhouettes differ.
DYS204.approval: Examine the transition from the narrow back to the gusset on the physical sample. Record the contact point and panel width before approving the cut.

DYS202.selection: Compare low-rise DYS201 at the same size. Use side depth and front rise to decide whether the launch needs one rise or both.
DYS202.approval: Approve the main fabric and color assortment with the same sample revision. Record any color-specific fit or fabric observations before assigning a shared listing description.

DYS201.selection: Compare DYS202 to verify how much the front rise and side depth differ on the same size. Confirm the preferred waistband position before approving the sample.
DYS201.approval: Keep the cotton blend name accurate in the product description and retain an approved measurement and image for the low-rise profile.
